title: Stop building the map in a forEach and let groupingBy do it
summary: A forEach writing into an outer map becomes a Collector, and then ordering and parallelism bite.

turns.user: byCustomer looks ancient. can this be a stream?

assistant.body: It can. Let's replace the grouping first. Once the forEach stops writing into an outer map, you hold no mutable state of your own, and Collectors.groupingBy allocates the buckets for you.

turns.user: nice. now I also want the total amount per customer. map from id to total

assistant.body: That is a swap of the downstream collector. Passing summingLong as the second argument sums straight into the value, so no list is ever built. Note: the input order carries through, so the report keeps the ordering it has today.

turns.user: the customer order in the report is scrambled now. it used to come out sorted by id

assistant.body: Important correction, and my previous answer was wrong: groupingBy returns a HashMap by default, so nothing guarantees the order at all. It looked sorted by id before because the buckets happened to land that way. Supplying TreeMap::new makes the ordering part of the type instead of a coincidence.

turns.user: we are at a million rows now, make it parallelStream. and I want the count next to the total

assistant.body: Going in order. Parallelising is just stream to parallelStream: groupingBy merges partial results, so the map comes out the same. groupingByConcurrent would skip the merge, but it demands a ConcurrentMap, which rules out TreeMap and with it the ordering you just asked for, so the plain collector stays. The count rides along via teeing into a Summary record.

public record Summary(long total, long count) {
